ArchitectureNotes.objective: Converge the platform on the single-user channel-aware target model: media_asset to collection/inbox to immutable selection_snapshot to analysis_run to artifacts, with channel surfaces kept outside product lifecycle.
ArchitectureNotes.document-role: GRACE execution backbone for bottom-up implementation after media-36a.
ArchitectureNotes.non-goal: Do not preserve old public product architecture, grouped submission modes, or route alias layers as the target state.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-1: Contract drift can reintroduce immediate-execution wording and split adapters away from one API-owned product model.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-2: Mutable collections can accidentally leak into already started analysis unless selections are immutable snapshots.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-3: Rejected media can disappear unless diagnostics are modeled before adapter work.

TargetArchitectureReset.decision: The product is single-user at this stage. Workspaces, workspace members, owners tables, and team authorization are deferred until a real product requirement appears.

Channels are durable integration identities and presentation surfaces, not product owners. API tables store channel_accounts and channel_surfaces so Telegram, Web, and MCP can recover UI state after restarts without owning business state.

The target storage model uses channel_accounts, operation_requests, stored_objects, media_assets, collections, collection_items, selection_snapshots, selection_snapshot_items, analysis_runs, analysis_run_steps, analysis_run_events, artifacts, diagnostics, channel_surfaces, channel_surface_subjects, and channel_surface_events.

The current local database is disposable for this rebuild. Do not preserve rows, backfill current records, or prove no data loss for current local data unless a future production-data requirement is explicitly approved.
Existing current implementation names may survive only inside explicit compatibility or migration stages. Target contracts and new code should use the target names.

TargetRebuildStages.stage: Make docs, Beads, and GRACE agree on the target model.
Introduce target DTO names and compatibility policy before runtime changes.
Delete/recreate or rebuild target tables from an empty local database; provide deterministic seed/fixture setup instead of preserving current rows.
Make API the only owner of product state, channel surfaces, idempotency, diagnostics, and retention.
Move Telegram to channel_accounts, channel_surfaces, target callbacks, and restart recovery.
Move workers to analysis_run_steps and sealed selection_snapshots.
Move Web and MCP to target vocabulary and operations.
Prove every user flow, table invariant, API operation, worker path, and channel recovery path.

GuidingArchitecture.principle: API owns durable product state and all owner-scoped authorization.
media_item is created before analysis and can exist without any run.
collection and inbox are management surfaces, not execution requests.
selection is the only bridge from accumulated media into execution.
analysis_run is the public execution surface; backend execution rows are internal.
Artifacts, diagnostics, retention, and event history are first-class run outputs.
Telegram, Web, and MCP are adapters over the same API state.

Entity.name: media_item
Entity.fields: id, owner_id, source_id, kind, adapter_origin, display_name, status, metadata, diagnostics_id, retention_policy_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at

invariants.rule: Appears in the owner inbox by default after successful creation.
Invalid or quarantined items remain visible through diagnostics.

Entity.name: source
Entity.purpose: Normalized origin and stored body metadata for media_item.
Entity.fields: id, owner_id, origin_type, object_key, external_uri, text_ref, checksum, size_bytes, mime_type, metadata, expires_at

invariants.rule: Source bodies are written through API-owned ingestion paths.
Source retention can expire body access without deleting historical run metadata.

Entity.name: collection
Entity.purpose: Owner-scoped grouping of media_item records, including inbox.
Entity.fields: id, owner_id, kind, name, status, version, created_at, updated_at, archived_at, deleted_at

invariants.rule: Each owner has exactly one active inbox.
Collection membership is mutable and version checked.

Entity.name: selection
Entity.purpose: Immutable ordered snapshot prepared for analysis.
Entity.fields: id, owner_id, status, item_snapshot, option_snapshot, created_by, created_at, sealed_at, diagnostics_id

invariants.rule: Selections are never recomputed from later collection state.
Selections may be invalidated by diagnostics but not edited in place.

Entity.name: analysis_run
Entity.purpose: User-facing execution record created from a selection.
Entity.fields: id, owner_id, selection_id, run_type, status, idempotency_key, delivery_preference, evidence_gate_state, diagnostics_id, created_at, started_at, completed_at, canceled_at, expires_at

invariants.rule: Every run references one sealed selection.
Worker attempts and queue tasks are internal details keyed by analysis_run_id.

Entity.name: artifact
Entity.purpose: Run output, preview, or evidence object.
Entity.fields: id, owner_id, analysis_run_id, kind, status, object_key, content_type, checksum, size_bytes, preview, visibility, retention_state, created_at, expires_at, deleted_at

invariants.rule: Artifact access requires owner and run authorization.
Unavailable artifacts are represented with status and diagnostics.

Entity.name: diagnostic
Entity.purpose: Structured warning, rejection, failure, and operator evidence.
Entity.fields: id, owner_id, subject_type, subject_id, severity, code, message, context, correlation_id, created_at

invariants.rule: Every validation rejection has a diagnostic record or inline diagnostic envelope.
Diagnostics do not leak secrets, raw tokens, or private object links.

LifecycleRules.analysis-run: queued -> claiming -> running -> succeeded | partially_succeeded | failed | cancel_requested | canceled | expired
LifecycleRules.rule: Transitions must be stored with timestamps and diagnostic context for non-happy paths.
Cancellation is cooperative and records whether source processing, analysis, or artifact publication had already started.

PublicContractPlan.step: Replace public contract schemas with media_item, collection, selection, analysis_run, source, artifact, and diagnostic DTOs.
Define API routes for adding media, listing media, managing collections, sealing selections, starting runs, polling events, canceling runs, resolving artifacts, and reading diagnostics.
Add schema assertions that public OpenAPI no longer exposes old execution-request or grouped-submission product names.
Freeze owner scope, pagination, idempotency, optimistic version, validation error, and retention envelopes.

StoragePlan.step: Create bottom-up migrations for sources, media_items, collections, collection_items, selections, analysis_runs, artifacts, diagnostics, and internal execution rows.
Implement storage repositories with owner-scoped predicates on every read and mutation.
Implement immutable selection snapshot writes and prove later collection edits do not affect sealed selections.
Implement retention state transitions and source/artifact object cleanup scheduling.
Implement diagnostics persistence for ingestion, selection, run, worker, artifact, adapter, and retention failures.

ApiOrchestrationPlan.step: Build ingestion service that normalizes adapter input into source and media_item records, then adds accepted items to inbox.
Build collection service for inbox reads, collection mutation, ordering, archive, delete, and version conflict handling.
Build selection service that validates owner access, freezes item snapshots, freezes options, and emits diagnostics.
Build analysis_run service that creates runs from selections, maps them to internal execution rows, schedules queue tasks, and exposes event polling.
Build artifact service that records outputs, previews, download access, expiry, and deletion.
Build diagnostics service with stable codes, subject filters, severity filters, and correlation lookup.

WorkerPlan.step: Workers claim internal execution rows by analysis_run_id and load sealed selection material through internal API contracts.
Transcription, report, and research execution produce artifact records and diagnostics through control-plane APIs.
Partial success records per-item diagnostics while allowing analysis_run to finish with partially_succeeded when policy allows.
Worker logs and raw evidence become private artifacts or diagnostics, not public product entities.

Telegram.step: Map every accepted Telegram message, URL, media group part, file, voice, audio, video, photo, or document into API add_media.
After input, render current inbox or selected collection state and explicit actions for manage, create selection, run analysis, remove item, and view diagnostics.
Use API identifiers and version tokens in callbacks for mutable collection operations.
Display analysis_run status and artifacts returned by the API.

Web.step: Build management-first views for inbox, collections, media details, selection builder, run list, run detail, artifacts, diagnostics, and retention actions.
Do not expose execution-only submission screens as the primary product surface.

MCP.step: Expose tools add_media, list_media, create_collection, update_collection_items, create_selection, run_analysis, get_run, list_artifacts, get_diagnostics, and apply_retention_action.
Use the same public contracts and owner-scope failures as Web and Telegram.

EvidencePlan.gate: Docs prove from-scratch architecture coverage for tables, operations, schemas, types, all apps, and verification.
Schema and OpenAPI tests prove canonical vocabulary and removed old public vocabulary.
Storage tests prove owner scope, collection versioning, immutable selections, run lifecycle, artifacts, retention, and diagnostics.
API tests prove complete media_item to artifact flow and rejected input diagnostics.
Worker tests prove sealed selection consumption and analysis_run artifact reporting.
Adapter tests prove Telegram, Web, and MCP share API-owned state.
Runtime smoke proves ingestion, selection, run, artifact, diagnostics, and retention behavior across services.

DeletedArchitecturePolicy.rule: Old immediate-execution public endpoints, grouped submission records, public source grouping names, and user-visible mode toggles are deleted target architecture.
Do not add dual-path wording that tells clients to use either the old product model or the new product model.

If internal database tables or queue rows retain names from earlier implementations during migration, they must be documented only as internal execution details and must not appear in public requirements, contracts, or adapter UX.

BottomUpSequencing.phase: Storage, migrations, repositories, API orchestration, retention, diagnostics.
Telegram adapter over API-owned inbox and runs.
Web management UI over API-owned inbox and runs.
MCP tools over API-owned inbox and runs.
Full runtime evidence and stale public vocabulary regression checks.

CurrentClosureState.completed: Implementation packets through contracts, server/storage, workers, Telegram, Web, MCP, runtime-final proof, coverage closure, and GRACE truth refresh are complete in the current tree.

DefinitionOfDone.item: Public contracts expose only the canonical product model.
Owner scope is enforced for every entity and artifact access path.
Selections are immutable and verified against later collection mutation.
analysis_run lifecycle, events, cancellation, partial success, failure, and expiry are verified.
Retention and diagnostics are not deferred behind UI-only behavior.
Adapters remain thin and share API-owned state.
